Ilmenite-type MgSiO3 structure from Horiuchi et al., Am. Mineral. 67, 788-793 (1982). The conventional hexagonal cell has Z=6; this is also the cell and volume basis used by the Reynard et al. (1996) and Siersch et al. (2021) EOS records.

## Automatic selections

- **Equilibrium:** [akimotoite\_siersch\_2021\_bm3\_1](#record-akimotoite_siersch_2021_bm3_1)
- **Hugoniot:** None

This is the ruby-pressure assignment of the same 16-row compression/decompression experiment represented by the companion ice-VII-scale record. It is a distinct fit, not a duplicate parameter transcription. The paper reports that V0 was varied and stayed within 0.01% of the measured in-cell value, while K0 was fixed at the adopted 212 GPa Brillouin value. Ruby-line broadening above 15 GPa showed increasing nonhydrostatic stress; the authors therefore regarded K0'=7.5 as less realistic than the ice-VII-scale result. The source gives neither parameter covariance nor a confidence convention for parenthesized fit errors, and it does not specify an exact ruby calibration equation. The numerical 298 K reference encodes the source's qualitative 'ambient temperature' wording rather than a measured sample temperature.

This is the authors' preferred pressure assignment of the same experiment represented by the companion ruby-scale record. It is a distinct fit, not a duplicate parameter transcription. Ice-VII (110) diffraction and MgSiO3 ilmenite were measured on the same 50 micrometer X-ray spot; Table 1 prints 12 finite-pressure Pi values, and Figure 3f additionally plots the two ambient measurements as zero-pressure anchors, giving 14 usable rows. The paper reports that V0 was varied and K0 was fixed at the adopted 212 GPa Brillouin value. Above 15 GPa the pressure medium developed nonhydrostatic stress and pressure gradients; the bracketed ice-pressure quantities are maximum gradient estimates, not stated one-sigma errors. The source gives neither parameter covariance nor a confidence convention for fitted-parameter errors. The numerical 298 K reference encodes the source's qualitative 'ambient temperature' wording rather than a measured sample temperature.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

An unweighted fit of all 55 Zhou KS(P,T) values closely recovers Zhou's reported linear coefficients, so weighting does not explain the Dorogokupets mismatch. The 298 K fits still do not reproduce the published K0/K0\_prime pair because the 2015 result is a joint thermal/acoustic optimization with an unstated residual construction and phase-specific fixed/free mask.

</details>

## Observation datasets

### akimotoite\_reynard\_1996\_table1\_compression

- **Description:** All 16 room-temperature MgSiO3 ilmenite unit-cell rows printed in Reynard et al. (1996) Table 1, with ruby and ice-VII pressure assignments and the measured ice-VII calibrant volumes.
- **Kind:** pressure\_volume\_lattice\_parameters\_with\_calibrant
- **Reference:**
    - **Authors:** Reynard; Fiquet; Itié; Rubie
    - **Year:** 1996
    - **Source:** American Mineralogist
    - **Volume:** 81
    - **Locator:** 45-50
    - **DOI:** 10.2138/am-1996-1-206
- **Source location:** Table 1, article page 46
- **Associated EOS records:** akimotoite\_reynard\_1996\_bm3\_ruby\_2; akimotoite\_reynard\_1996\_bm3\_ice\_vii\_3
- **Uncertainty:**
    - **Reported as:** Cell-parameter and MgSiO3 volume parentheses are estimated one-standard-deviation values. Ruby-pressure brackets are estimates from fluorescence line widths. Ice-pressure brackets are maximum pressure gradients estimated from ice-VII diffraction-line widths, and ice-volume parentheses are peak-location estimates described as probably underestimated.
    - **Covariance:** not\_reported
- **Notes:** The table's Pr and Pi columns are retained separately because they define two published BM3 fits. Blank Pi/Vice entries remain null in the transcription. The 16 rows include 13 compression states, two decompression states, and a final decompressed ambient state; together with the initial ambient row this gives 16 observations. Table 1 prints 12 finite-pressure Pi values; Figure 3f also plots the two ambient measurements as zero-pressure anchors, giving 14 rows for the ice-VII-scale reproduction. At Pr=0.95 GPa, the printed a=4.7240 A and c=13.491 A imply V=260.732 A^3 rather than the printed 260.49 A^3; all values are retained verbatim and the EOS reproduction uses the V column. No official supplement or machine-readable deposit was found; this CSV is a direct transcription of the final article table.

[Observation resource](https://github.com/CPrescher/peritheos/blob/main/peritheos/data/datasets/akimotoite-reynard-1996-table1-compression.csv)
— SHA-256 `5013e95e53e8e8fa08e1fa7ee59b6f85fb0bb84c3b689c2d0665590a47b505d3`.

- **Description:** Recoverable 298 K akimotoite slice of the Dorogokupets et al. joint optimization, including Wang and preserving both non-independent Reynard ruby and ice-VII pressure assignments.

    - **Authors:** Dorogokupets; Dymshits; Sokolova; Danilov; Litasov

- **Associated EOS records:** akimotoite\_dorogokupets\_2015\_298k\_rydberg\_stacey
- **Uncertainty:**
    - **Weights:** No 2015 point-weighting rule is stated. The primary diagnostic is unweighted; sensitivity weights use source error/spread fields plus projected volume uncertainty. Ice-VII brackets are maximum gradients, not one-sigma errors.

- **Notes:** This is a partial fit reconstruction, not the full joint thermoelastic optimization.
